correctness.rationale: At m=N-1 row i of the unshuffled integer incidence matrix omits exactly N-1-i. Shuffling columns consequently gives J-Q, with q=sigma composed with the reversal and hence all q equally represented. Constants contribute m and on the invariant zero-sum subspace the action is -Q, giving the displayed cycle polynomial after removing one t+1. Thus for d>=2 occurrence of a fixed primitive phase is equivalent to the presence of a cycle of length divisible by d. The exponential generating function for avoidance is (1-z^d)^(1/d)/(1-z), whose binomial partial sum at floor(N/d) gives the product. Order 1 is separate because one constant eigenvector was removed: exactly the single-cycle permutations lack -1/m. The coarse finite Markov eigenvalues are genuine piecewise constant BV eigenvalues (changing the row/column convention transposes without changing spectrum). The source's proven upper bound equals the essential radius 1/m in this family. A cycle of length N-1 gives a phase on the mixing-rate circle, not among the listed conjectural vertices; for even N the additional sign is itself an N-th root and for odd N the common sign cancels in the comparison. Strict convexity of the disk excludes this phase from their hull. This refutes the literal v3 hull statement and its maximal-radius consequence, not the proven rate bound or a modified statement about isolated eigenvalues outside the essential disk. The result describes the finite matrix, not the entire BV spectrum.
correctness.reproduction: In the 0-based N=4 case take sigma=(3,0,2,1). Multiplying the incidence and permutation matrices gives rows (1,0,1,1), (1,1,0,1), (0,1,1,1), (1,1,1,0); the omitted-column permutation is (1,2,0,3), type (3,1). The characteristic polynomial is (t-3)(t+1)(t^2-t+1) and (1-i*sqrt(3))/6 lies outside the predicted diamond. As a bounded exact check, the five N=4 cycle types 1^4, 2 1^2, 2^2, 3 1, 4 have sizes 1,6,3,8,6; orders 1,2,3,4 then have incidence counts 18,15,8,6, agreeing with the formula. The frozen permutation-enumeration script was inspected, not run; the argument for general N is algebraic and does not depend on finite enumeration.
